best_for: People who already pay for a VPN and want a browser that makes them look like every other user, without routing traffic through Tor.
description:
Mullvad Browser comes from Mullvad VPN AB, a Swedish company in Gothenburg that is owned by its two founders. Mullvad says it earns nothing from the browser. Its income comes from its VPN service, and the browser is meant as a companion to it.

The idea behind it is to hide in the crowd. Big tech firms, data brokers and authorities can tell people apart by the small details their browser gives away. Mullvad Browser works to make those details match for everyone who uses it, so you look like one of many. If the topic is new to you, Mullvad's site has plain guides on what a browser fingerprint is and how a VPN guards against mass surveillance.

points.title: Tor Browser without the Tor network
points.text: The Tor Project builds it for Mullvad. You get the same anti-fingerprinting work, such as letterboxing, but traffic goes straight out over your own connection or VPN.

points.title: Your IP address still shows
points.text: The browser hides your fingerprint, not your address. Mullvad itself says to pair it with a VPN you trust; any VPN works, not only Mullvad's.

points.title: Free, and no VPN subscription needed
points.text: The browser costs nothing and is MPL-2.0 open source. Mullvad says telemetry has been removed.

points.title: Private mode is always on
points.text: Cookies are not kept between sessions, and third-party cookies are kept in separate jars while you browse. Expect to log in again each time you open it.

points.title: Deliberately few add-ons
points.text: uBlock Origin comes built in. Mullvad keeps extra tracker blocking out on purpose, because each added blocker makes you stand out from other users. Grey bars around pages are the letterboxing doing its job.

points.title: Windows installs per user
points.text: The Windows installer is x64 only and installs for the current user. The Windows listing keeps 49 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.

points.title: The Flatpak is not Flathub-verified
points.text: The Linux Flatpak names Mullvad VPN AB as developer and runs on x64 and Arm64, but Flathub does not mark it as verified.
